source.title: Towards Foundation Models for Scientific Machine Learning: Characterizing Scaling and Transfer Behavior
source.authors: Shashank Subramanian; Peter Harrington; Kurt Keutzer; W. Bhimji; D. Morozov; Michael W. Mahoney; Amir Gholami; E. Pd

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study explores parameter scaling and transfer in scientific machine learning, a different setting from language-model pretraining. It does not fit or test the power laws, compute-optimal allocation, or other specific claim versions here.
record.gate_note: The paper reports FNO parameter-scale and downstream-transfer results, but measures relative L2 error on PDE solutions rather than held-out language-model cross-entropy. Its scaling experiments do not fit power laws or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. It cites language-model scaling work as motivation. Rows below record the directly reported scientific-model scaling outcomes as findings that fit no listed version.
record.test_reason: The study scales Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) parameter count (64K to 256M) and downstream data for PDE surrogate models. It reports only qualitative monotonic drops in relative L2 error, with no power-law fit, extrapolation, compute-optimal analysis, fixed-parameter shape sweep or language-model loss. Its results therefore cannot show whether the power-law form (V5) or any other version holds. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as motivation. The reader's T3 implies a result on the claim, which this study does not give, so it is reclassified as T6/discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that pre-training and fine-tuning FNOs beats training from scratch, especially with limited downstream data and under small-to-moderate distribution shift. They also conclude that fine-tuning gains grow with model size and that a single model pre-trained on mixed PDE operators transfers across tasks. They make no power-law claims.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales FNO parameter counts from 64K to 256M and measures PDE relative L2 error and transfer behavior. It does not use language-model held-out cross-entropy, sweep training tokens or compute, fit scaling laws, or determine compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Model scale and downstream-data amount are varied. The paper also reports tuning learning rates by model and dataset size, and states that input normalization is critical; it does not test how these choices affect language-model scaling-law fits.

fits_no_version.finding: For FNOs on SYS-1 and SYS-2 (medium OOD), error saturates above 1e-2 at 64K parameters. It drops monotonically with model size up to 256M, and fine-tuning gains grow with size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For FNO PDE surrogates, downstream relative L2 error falls monotonically with parameter count (64K to 256M), and pre-training/fine-tuning benefits grow with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream test error falls monotonically with the number of downstream examples. Transfer learning reaches 1e-2 error with about 64 examples versus about 8K from scratch, with diminishing returns near pre-training dataset size (Fig. 3, §4 Q1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For FNO PDE surrogates, pre-training cuts the downstream data needed for a target error by about 100x, with gains vanishing as downstream data approaches pre-training size.

record.problems: The study uses only FNOs and PDE relative L2 error, not language-model cross-entropy. It does not fit power laws or sweep compute and token counts. Model-scale curve values are mainly presented in figures rather than as numerical values; the paper reports seed variability for selected transfer experiments, not the parameter-scaling curves.
record.rows_left_out: Fig. 4 contains further figure-only curve values across downstream-data amounts and intermediate parameter scales. These are not separately extracted because the study does not provide numerical values for those points and they do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Held-out language-model loss as a power law in parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation from small fitted runs to much larger runs.
Shape effects at fixed parameter count. The study scales d and m together with parameter count, so shape is never held fixed.
Whether a power-law form holds for scientific (PDE) models or under fine-tuning/transfer. Error falls monotonically with model and data size, but no power law is fitted or assessed.
Downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of exponents or splits on fitting choices, and bending away from a single power law.

record.verdict_notes: Downstream-data scaling results (Fig. 3, Fig. 5, Appendix B.1) are not in the rows. They are recorded here under fits_no_version, since they also fit no version. All scaling curves are figure-only, with no fitted exponents.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations and their growth with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or regimes; the study does not fit or evaluate power-law forms.
Predictability of language-model downstream performance with scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.
